final_candidates.decision_summary: Replacing the aromatic residue with proline is likely to disrupt local backbone geometry and hydrophobic packing in the structured N-terminal region.
Proline insertion in the central structured segment should strongly perturb backbone conformation and destabilize PsaE folding.
Introducing a charged aspartate at this hydrophobic central position is expected to impair core packing and reduce folding stability.

stop_reason.detail: The current top three are well differentiated by plausible folding-disruption mechanisms, and no external evidence is available to refine them.

history.rationale: Proline substitution at a conserved aromatic/hydrophobic position is likely to disrupt local secondary structure and packing. The large conformational constraint makes this a strong folding-disruption candidate.
Retained as the leading candidate because proline substitution at a conserved-looking aromatic position is likely to disrupt local backbone geometry and folding.
A proline substitution at a conserved-looking aromatic site is likely to disrupt local secondary structure and packing. It remains the strongest folding-disruption candidate.

Introducing proline into the central hydrophobic segment may break a structured strand or helix and weaken the compact fold. The WT isoleucine suggests this position normally supports hydrophobic packing.
Retained because introducing proline within the central structured region should strongly perturb secondary structure and destabilize the small subunit.
Introducing proline within the central structured region should strongly perturb backbone geometry and destabilize the small subunit. It remains a high-priority candidate.
Replacing a hydrophobic valine with a charged aspartate in the structured middle region should create an unfavorable polarity/packing mismatch. This may substantially destabilize the small subunit.
Retained because replacing hydrophobic valine with a charged aspartate may disrupt hydrophobic packing in the folded core.

Replacing a hydrophobic residue in the central hydrophobic stretch with charged aspartate may disrupt core packing and introduce an unfavorable electrostatic environment. It remains among the best non-proline destabilizing substitutions.
Proline at this hydrophobic position could introduce a backbone kink and disrupt local structure. It is a plausible destabilizing change without relying solely on charge burial.
Retained as a high-impact proline substitution in the N-terminal structured region, though ranked below W17P because local structural context is uncertain.
This proline could disrupt the transition into the central region, but its effect is less certain because the local segment may be flexible.
This aromatic residue lies within a compact hydrophobic-looking region, and proline would remove aromatic packing while constraining the backbone. The combined effects are expected to impair folding.
Retained because proline can disrupt backbone regularity and the substitution also removes an aromatic side chain that may contribute to packing.
Proline at position 34 is potentially disruptive, although its proximity to native Pro35 makes the structural effect less predictable than at W17 or I32.
The C-terminal leucine may contribute to terminal packing, while proline could disrupt the end of a structured element. Destabilization is plausible despite the terminal location.
Retained as a possible C-terminal folding disruptor, although terminal flexibility makes its effect less certain than central proline substitutions.
C-terminal proline could perturb terminal secondary structure, but terminal flexibility makes its folding impact less certain.

Introducing a negatively charged residue at a hydrophobic position in the central region may produce an unfavorable buried-charge or packing defect. This is a strong alternative to proline-based disruption.
Retained because introducing charge at a hydrophobic isoleucine may impair core packing and destabilize the fold.
A hydrophobic-to-acidic change may impair packing, but it is less directly backbone-disruptive than proline substitutions.
Aspartate substitution changes a hydrophobic valine to a charged residue within the structured core-like segment. The resulting polarity mismatch could weaken the fold.
Retained as a hydrophobic-to-charged perturbation in the structured N-terminal half, with moderate confidence due to uncertain burial.
The charge insertion may destabilize a hydrophobic environment, though the magnitude depends on whether this position is solvent exposed.
Proline would remove an aromatic side chain and impose backbone rigidity near the central hydrophobic region. This combination may interfere with local packing and secondary structure.
Retained because proline may disrupt the local backbone and removal of phenylalanine could weaken hydrophobic packing.
Proline may disrupt the central-to-C-terminal structural transition, but loss of an aromatic side chain and local backbone context make the outcome uncertain.
Changing leucine to aspartate may disrupt hydrophobic packing in the C-terminal half. It is a lower-confidence candidate because the local structural environment is less certain.
Retained as a lower-confidence hydrophobic-to-charged destabilization in the C-terminal region.
The hydrophobic-to-acidic substitution could weaken packing, but the glycine/asparagine-rich neighborhood may already be flexible and reduce its impact.
